collection_plan.rationale: Frozen objective: minimize median aligned max-rank step_ms for one accumulated DDP step (2 ranks, fp32 GPT-2 124M, bucket_cap_mb=25), with diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms as a secondary goal. The torch collector already ran and supplies that diagnostic: 13 bucket allreduces (12 x 28,351,488 B + 1 x 157,541,376 B, float32, process_group 0) with communication_kernel_sum_ms = 192.994 on rank 0 vs 33.219 on rank 1, compute_overlap_ms 7.81/2.05, payload coverage 13/13, and bucket identity already established by observed gradient-storage membership plus matched parameter inventory; re-listing torch would add nothing. The decisive open question is the ~6x rank asymmetry in otherwise identical collective sequences: rank-0 kernels (14.2-17.2 ms per 27 MB bucket) vs rank-1 sum of 33.2 ms, i.e. wait versus transfer. Three collectors resolve exactly that, within the frozen workload: (1) nccl_tuning, because kernel entry names (ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL) alone do not identify the actual algorithm/protocol decision for 27 MB and 150 MB messages over the observed SHM/direct/direct 2-channel transport in a warmed worker; (2) collective_calibration, which runs a warmed synthetic full-world SUM allreduce at the actually observed sizes/dtypes with correctness checks, giving a reference duration per size to compare against the observed per-kernel durations (reference experiment, not a performance lower bound or critical-path estimate); (3) execution_timeline, whose separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, clock alignment bounds for matched CPU submissions, per-device intervals and synchronization events can attribute the asymmetry to submission skew between ranks without replacing any communication hook and without subtracting timestamps across rank clocks. Excluded: nsys (optional) because per-rank overlap is already quantified by torch, no graph tracing question exists (eager attention, no CUDA graphs), and nsys timelines alone cannot separate NCCL waiting from wire transfer or prove bucket identity, which is already observed; device_telemetry because its device-wide NVML rates/utilization have native windows not aligned to operator ranges and are not per-collective bytes, and NVLink is unsupported (NVML status 3) while transport is SHM, so it cannot change the decision; python_runtime because host dispatch is not implicated by any observation and its perturbing cProfile times are not clean scores; candidate_diagnostics and binding_cost because no candidate exists yet (binding_cost also re-runs in candidate resource feedback once applicable).
